introSlide.heading: How well do you know Asia's tax rules?
introSlide.description: 4 questions. Most digital nomads get at least 1 wrong.

slides.heading: Q1: Stay 184 days in Korea and you owe tax on worldwide income
A1: TRUE
slides.description: 183+ days = automatic tax resident. 6-45% on ALL income, including foreign clients. No opt-in.

slides.heading: Q2: Japan's DN visa taxes you after 183 days
A2: FALSE
slides.description: Non-resident status is baked into the visa design. 6 months, 0% tax on foreign income.

slides.heading: Q3: Taiwan's tax recalculation at day 184 is retroactive
A3: TRUE
slides.description: Stay 183 days at flat 18%. Stay 1 extra day: your ENTIRE year moves to 5-40% graduated rates.

slides.heading: Q4: Taiwan Gold Card holders pay 0% tax
A4: FALSE
slides.description: 50% exemption on salary ABOVE NT$3M only, first 5 years. You still pay on the rest.

endingSlide.heading: How many did you get right?
endingSlide.description: 4/4: you track your days. 2-3: reread before your next trip. 0-1: hire a tax pro this month. Not tax advice. Consult a qualified tax professional. Follow @localnomad.club

caption:
Most digital nomads don't track their days. That mistake can cost $25,000.

Korea: cross 183 days and you're automatically a tax resident. 6-45% on worldwide income, including what you earn from foreign clients. No opt-in, no warning. The clock just runs.

Japan: the DN visa keeps you non-resident by design. 6 months, 0% tax on foreign income. Completely different outcome for the same duration.

Taiwan: the trap is retroactive. Plan a 180-day stay at the flat 18% rate. Stay 4 extra days. Your entire year's income moves to graduated 5-40% rates from day 1.

Gold Card doesn't mean 0% tax either. It's a 50% exemption on salary above NT$3M only.
